Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3392; unsoiled, i.e. (figuratively) pure:--undefiled.
BiblicalUsage: Unsoiled, undefiled, and the New Testament uses it for the things that stay clean. The inheritance is incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you. The high priest is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners. Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled; and pure religion and undefiled before God is this, to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe undefiled is the word for what the world cannot stain, and the four uses agree on what it is: the inheritance kept in heaven, the priest set apart, the marriage bed honoured, and the religion that visits the widow. The world soils by contact, and God keeps by separation — not the separation that hides, but the one that serves. I hold that the cleanest thing in the New Testament is not the man who avoids the world but the one who goes into it to visit the fatherless and comes back unspotted.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; James, Brother of Jesus
